purpose: Isradipine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering your blood pressure helps reduce your risk of having a stroke, heart attack, or kidney problems. Your doctor may prescribe it alone or along with other blood pressure medications.
how_it_works: Your blood vessels have tiny channels that let calcium flow in, which causes them to squeeze tight and raise your blood pressure. Isradipine blocks those calcium channels, which helps your blood vessels relax and widen. When your vessels are more relaxed, your heart does not have to work as hard and your blood pressure goes down.
common_side_effects: Flushing or feeling warm in your face, headache, dizziness, swelling in your ankles or feet, fast heartbeat, and stomach upset. These are usually mild and may improve after your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as your blood pressure could spike. Tell your doctor if you have heart problems, liver disease, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Avoid drinking large amounts of grapefruit juice, as it can increase the drug in your body and raise your risk of side effects. Stand up slowly to avoid feeling dizzy or lightheaded.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 2.5 mg taken twice a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose up to 10 mg twice a day depending on how well your blood pressure is controlled. The extended-release version (DynaCirc CR) is taken once daily. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
